thread:
elaine (support): Customer (AcmePayments) reporting very short/garbled completions after an automated regional switch. They say request latency spiked ~2s -> 800ms then outputs truncated and some tokens look split (eg. \"pay ment\"). Also billing shows zero token cost for some of those requests. They replayed with `curl` and attached request_id=rc_20260317_9a8b7c.
omar (sre): Noted. I see an automated region failover at 2026-03-17T08:22:12Z from eu-west -> ap-southeast in the routing logs (deploy-bot flagged). Could be serving a lighter/quantized variant in APAC.
deploy-bot: Region failover triggered for route: customer-eu -> ap-southeast (reason: auth-probe timeout). Event id: evt_2468123456.
kevin (runtime): I pulled the serving logs for rc_20260317_9a8b7c: runtime served model `rwd-7b-realtime` in eu-west until 08:22:12, then `rwd-7b-lite-q4` in ap-southeast for the retry. The lite-q4 variant uses a different tokenizer config (byte-level vs wordpiece) and smaller vocab, which explains token splitting.
elaine (support): Customer says they never asked for lite variant; they expect full `rwd-7b-realtime`. Is the routing policy allowed to fallback to a quantized variant with different tokenizer?
omar (sre): By default our standby policy will route to a compatible variant ID but compatibility is defined by model family, not tokenizer config. This is an oversight. I can reproduce the tokenization diff locally with the served checkpoints.
kevin (runtime): Repro steps for engineering: 1) send original prompt header: `--model rwd-7b-realtime --client-region eu-west` 2) simulate auth probe failure 3) observe retry served by `rwd-7b-lite-q4`. Quick check: run

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-lite-q4","input":"Payment of $AMOUNT to account 1234"}'
```

and compare tokenization to `rwd-7b-realtime`.
maria (billing): About billing showing zero token cost: I see gateway accepted the retry with status 200 but with `billing.skip=true` on the retry path due to a specific error code from our auth-probe detector. That's why some retries got no token charges. Need to confirm whether we retro-charge.
ryan (eng-product): This is product-impacting. We shouldn't silently swap to a tokenizer-incompatible variant. Suggest: 1) block cross-variant tokenizers on fallback, 2) add a routing header `x-variant-tokenizer` and 3) surface a `served-variant` field in API responses so customers see what was used.
elaine (support): Customer asks for repro steps they can run and for a mitigation so they can avoid bad outputs in the short term.
kevin (runtime): Short-term mitigation: add query param `prefer_same_tokenizer=true` — I'll hotfix routing policy for the next 30m to prefer exact tokenizer match when model_family == requested. For immediate repro, ask customer to set `model=rwd-7b-realtime` and `region_hint=eu-west` and include `retry_mode=none` to avoid automatic retry to standby. Example curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-realtime","input":"Transfer $100 to Vendor X","region_hint":"eu-west","retry_mode":"none"}'
```

That will force no client-side retry and should prevent the lite variant being used.
omar (sre): I'll also add a quick guard in the routing service: if candidate.variant.tokenizer != requested.variant.tokenizer then mark as incompatible for fallback. Deploying a fix to canary now.
maria (billing): For billing gaps: I'll open a ticket to evaluate retro-charging for requests where `billing.skip=true` was set erroneously. For immediate customer relief — we can credit the affected invoices. Please send me the list of request_ids.
elaine (support): I've asked the customer to run the `prefer_same_tokenizer` and `retry_mode=none` repro steps and sent instructions. I also requested logs and the exact request timestamps.
kevin (runtime): follow-up: I pushed the canary that blocks tokenizer-incompatible fallbacks (route-guard v2) to ap-southeast; monitoring shows no more lite-q4 switches for retried requests. Will roll to global in 10m if green.
ryan (eng-product): Can we add a visible response header like `X-Served-Variant: rwd-7b-lite-q4` so customers can triage? If yes, let's spec it and include in the product change.
elaine (support): Customer confirmed they saw `prefer_same_tokenizer` working and outputs restored when we forced `retry_mode=none`. They've accepted a billing credit offer pending billing ticket. Closing loop once canary is global. :thumbsup:
